name: smartctl
description: Reads S.M.A.R.T. self-monitoring data from disks: reallocated sectors, pending sectors, temperature, and overall health. Requires root.

flags.description: Just the overall health verdict: PASSED or FAILED.
Run a self-test (short ~2 min, long = hours).

examples.output: SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED
examples.explanation: The quick verdict. FAILED means the disk reports imminent failure — replace it.
Reallocated sector count: 0 is ideal; a growing number means the disk is remapping bad sectors and will eventually fail.
Starts a short self-test; check results with smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda.

about: SMART attributes are vendor-specific but a few are universal health indicators: 05 Reallocated_Sector_Ct, 197 Current_Pending_Sector, 198 Offline_Uncorrectable. Any nonzero pending/reallocated value rising over time predicts failure. SMART must be enabled (smartctl -s on) and monitored — it does nothing by itself.
useCases: Predict disk failures before they happen.
mistakes: Trusting PASSED alone — a disk can pass while pending sectors grow; read the attributes.
warnings: A "PASSED" verdict does not guarantee health; monitor attribute trends. RAID controllers often hide SMART data behind -d megaraid,N or -d sat.
